items.paper: says chosen reward one-hot but also states seven-dimensional input
items.source_code: one scalar equal to upper-network max Q

items.paper: two 10-unit hidden layers in the upper network and two 50-unit hidden layers in the lower network
items.source_code: three 10-unit upper hidden layers and seven 50-unit lower hidden layers

items.paper: final-completion formula is not fully defined for unfinished jobs
items.source_code: workload pressure using OPT plus ETL versus due window
items.note: paper_repro uses the only executable source interpretation for state/reward, while final evaluation uses the paper completion-time metric

items.paper: FIFO/EDD/MRT/SPT/LPT names are given, but neither the machine decoder nor the exact SPT/LPT workload scope is uniquely specified
items.resolution: FIFO uses arrival time; EDD uses absolute due date; MRT uses total remaining nominal work; SPT/LPT use the next operation's mean eligible-machine nominal time; all five use earliest predicted completion under the active profile and are labelled FIFO+ECT, EDD+ECT, MRT+ECT, SPT+ECT, LPT+ECT
items.note: predicted completion includes setup only when the active profile enables source tool-change semantics and never samples PM/CM inside a rule score

items.paper_and_code: corrective maintenance is sampled before processing and delays the operation; no within-operation interruption is implemented
items.note: do not claim physical within-operation breakdown interruption in the original-conference rerun

items.paper: the method section defines the state features but does not state that the first observation is an all-zero vector
items.source_code: training starts from an explicit six-dimensional zero vector rather than querying the environment

items.topic: paper A2 priority for unfinished jobs
items.paper: uses completion/tardiness notation that is not uniquely defined for an unfinished job at a constructive decision epoch
items.source_code: uses the current constructive completion proxy and a differently parenthesized urgency expression

resolution.paper_repro: use decision_time as the overdue completion proxy and reproduce the printed non-overdue expression
resolution.corrected_smc: use decision_time as the overdue completion proxy and projected/remaining-work values for state diagnostics

items.note: all three implementations must be separately named and unit-tested; do not hide this choice behind Rule 4/5/6 labels

items.paper: claims insertion into the earliest feasible idle slot
items.source_code: sets earliest_start no earlier than the machine tail, which makes historical gaps unreachable in normal execution
items.note: retrospective insertion is deferred because health-dependent durations and maintenance would require chronological replay of later machine events; do not implement an internally inconsistent partial fix

items.paper: the formulation assumes setup times are negligible and the printed B1/B2 equations do not include setup
items.source_code: change_cutter() adds a machine-specific tool-change delay when either the job changes machine or the machine changes job
items.note: paper_repro emits no SETUP interval; corrected_smc keeps explicit source tool-change costs as an audited correction

items.paper: Table I states 1=highest and 3=lowest, while the experimental table caption reverses the wording
items.source_code: the due-window formula and rule denominators behave as 1=high, 2=medium, 3=low
items.resolution: all profiles use 1=high, 2=medium, 3=low and preserve that meaning in metadata, tests, weights, and rule formulas

items.topic: absolute due date versus due window
items.paper: the printed equation omits the arrival-time addition
items.source_code: initial jobs use arrival zero and dynamic jobs use arrival + urgency-scaled estimated work
items.resolution: all stored due dates are absolute; for every job use arrival_time + (0.2 + 0.5*urgency)*estimated_work, and subtract arrival only when a relative due window is required
